controls.name: Discovery exit gate
controls.description: A deal cannot move to Proposal until scope, a specific decision maker, budget and a dated close are confirmed.
controls.evidence: HubSpot deal stage history and required deal properties

controls.name: Loss reason recorded
controls.description: The reason for a loss is written in the HubSpot deal notes before the deal is set to Closed Lost.
controls.evidence: HubSpot deal notes

controls.name: Partner signs SOW first
controls.description: Every SOW goes out by e-signature envelope with the Partner as signer 1. The Partner's signature is the review and approval; the client cannot see the SOW until it is signed.
controls.evidence: E-signature envelope audit trail

controls.name: Void and re-sign on any change
controls.description: Any change requested in Negotiation voids the envelope. The service line owner revises the quote in Halo and the Partner signs the new version first.
controls.evidence: Voided and reissued envelopes; Halo quote revisions

controls.name: XO handoff acceptance
controls.description: The XO confirms the auto-created project and sales order match the executed SOW and records acceptance in Halo. Sales hands the work to Operations only after acceptance.
controls.evidence: Halo acceptance field / action on the project

controls.name: Partner signs change orders first
controls.description: Every change order is signed by the Partner (Account Executive Owner) before it reaches the client, and out-of-scope work starts only after the client signs.
controls.evidence: Signed change order envelope; revised Halo project budget
controls.flag: Partner signs every change order before the client.

controls.name: Client acceptance before closeout
controls.description: A project is closed only after the client's written acceptance of the deliverables (an email is enough) is recorded on the Halo project.
controls.evidence: Client's acceptance email attached to the Halo project

controls.name: Priority and SLA set at triage
controls.owner: Managed Technology dispatcher; Service Desk Tier 1
controls.description: Every ticket gets a category and priority at triage, which starts the matching SLA timers in Halo.
controls.evidence: Halo SLA reports

controls.name: Out-of-scope work approved first
controls.description: Work outside the managed services agreement starts only after the XO approves it and the client accepts the quote or T&M estimate in Halo.
controls.evidence: XO approval and client acceptance recorded on the Halo ticket or quote

controls.name: Billable time approved
controls.description: Billable time and expenses, due by end of day Friday each week, are approved by the Project Controller / XO before they can be invoiced.
controls.evidence: Halo timesheet approvals
controls.flag: Practice lead approves each timesheet for completeness by Monday end of day; the XO then approves billable time on their clients before invoicing.

controls.name: Invoice approved by XO / Project Controller
controls.description: The XO or Project Controller reviews and approves each invoice before the AR Clerk runs and sends it.
controls.evidence: Invoice approval in Halo

controls.name: Halo-to-QBO invoice sync reconciled
controls.description: Each invoice run, invoice counts and totals in Halo are reconciled to QuickBooks Online.
controls.evidence: Sync reconciliation report

controls.name: Sales tax calculated by Avalara
controls.description: Avalara adds estimated sales tax to quotes and calculates final sales tax on invoices in Halo; QuickBooks Online and Avalara handle filing and remittance. Tax is never keyed by hand.
controls.evidence: Avalara transaction log

controls.name: Finance spot-check of invoice run
controls.description: Before each invoice run is sent, Finance spot-checks the run summary (totals and exceptions) after XO approval.
controls.evidence: Invoice run summary with Finance sign-off

controls.name: Cash application reconciled
controls.description: Payments applied to invoices are reconciled to bank deposits.
controls.evidence: QBO bank reconciliation

controls.name: Monthly AR aging review
controls.description: The Next Level Now controller reviews AR aging each month, and XOs review their past-due accounts.
controls.evidence: Reviewed AR aging report

controls.name: Credit hold approval
controls.owner: Managing Partner, Operations and account EO
controls.description: A credit hold or service suspension, considered at 90+ days past due, requires joint approval from the Managing Partner over Operations and the account EO.
controls.evidence: Approval recorded on the client in Halo

controls.name: Write-off approval
controls.description: Every bad-debt write-off is approved by the CEO (no dollar threshold today) before the Controller posts it.
controls.evidence: Approved write-off memo; QBO journal entry

controls.name: Approved time locked
controls.description: Approved time entries are locked in Halo; a change requires the approver to reopen the entry, so billed and reported hours cannot be altered silently.
controls.evidence: Halo timesheet approval and edit history

controls.name: Seat counts from the client's access review
controls.description: Per-user quantities on recurring agreements change only at the quarterly QBR, using the user count the client confirmed in its user access review.
controls.evidence: Client-confirmed quarterly user access review; Halo agreement change history

controls.name: Leadership approves the monthly close
controls.description: The CEO and the Managing Partner over Operations review the monthly P&L and balance sheet before Next Level Now finalizes the close.
controls.evidence: Approved monthly statements (email or sign-off) per month

controls.name: Closed periods locked
controls.description: After approval, Next Level Now sets the password-protected closing date in QuickBooks Online so closed months cannot change without it.
controls.evidence: QuickBooks Online closing date settings and audit log

controls.name: Renewal price changes approved
controls.description: Any renewal price increase, within the contract's annual cap, is approved by the Managing Partner over Operations before the XO tells the client.
controls.evidence: Approval recorded on the Halo renewal ticket; written client notice

controls.name: Below-floor pricing approved
controls.description: A quote priced below the price-book floor cannot be sent until the Managing Partner over Operations approves it.
controls.evidence: Halo quote approval history
controls.flag: Quotes priced below the floor are held in Halo until the Managing Partner over Operations approves them.

controls.name: Vendor bank details verified by call-back
controls.description: New vendor bank details, and any change to them, are confirmed by calling a known vendor contact before they are used.
controls.evidence: Call-back log on the vendor record

controls.name: CEO releases the payment run
controls.description: Each weekly payment run of budget-owner-approved bills is approved and released by the CEO.
controls.evidence: Approved payment run per week

controls.name: Pass-through costs reconciled to billings
controls.description: Each month, Pax8 and distributor costs are reconciled to the matching Halo invoice lines so no pass-through cost goes unbilled.
controls.evidence: Monthly pass-through reconciliation

3.5.1.title: Manage leads and opportunities
3.5.1.summary: Everything runs in HubSpot; a tier-1 hand-raiser skips the BDR qualification call.

steps.title: Start: inbound signal or ICP fit
Create lead
steps.detail: Tier-1 is a rules-based HubSpot property set from firmographics (employee band, vertical, metro).

steps.title: Tier-1 and hand-raiser?
steps.detail: A hand-raiser has reached out to us looking to do work.

steps.title: Qualification call
steps.detail: Confirms the lead fits and is warm. Warm criteria are not yet documented (open item).

steps.title: End: not qualified, nurture in HubSpot
Book discovery
steps.detail: Booking the discovery meeting creates the deal record at the Discovery stage.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.note: Scope, decision maker, budget, close date
steps.detail: All vetting happens here: scope, a specific decision maker, budget and a time-bound close date.

steps.title: Record loss
steps.detail: Loss reason in deal notes. Still-ideal-fit accounts get the nurture tag (replacing the Warm 250).

steps.title: End: closed lost, nurture tag if ideal fit

3.5.3.title: Develop and manage proposals and quotes
3.5.3.summary: Operations builds the SOW in Halo; the Partner signs first; any change voids the envelope and reissues it.

steps.title: Opportunity created
steps.note: Halo opp synced to HubSpot deal

steps.title: Build quote and SOW
steps.detail: One quote and one SOW. On multi-service-line deals the Partner coordinates the service line owners; lines are tagged by service line. Avalara is integrated with Halo so quotes carry estimated sales tax.

steps.title: Partner signs first
steps.detail: The Partner is signer 1 on the envelope; the signature is the review and approval.

steps.title: Void and revise
steps.detail: The envelope is voided and the quote revised in Halo. Revisions trigger no integration push.

3.5.4.title: Manage sales orders
3.5.4.summary: Halo builds the records; the XO runs the handoff and accepts it, which hands the work from Sales to Operations.

steps.title: Auto-create records
steps.note: Project per service line, sales order

steps.title: Handoff call
steps.detail: Internal sales-to-delivery handoff. Partner attendance is required.

steps.title: Attend handoff
steps.detail: Transfers client context and any commitments made outside the SOW.

steps.title: End: handed to Operations (5.4 Deliver service)

5.4.title: Deliver service to customer
5.4.summary: Project delivery for professional and technical work: plan, kick off, deliver, handle scope changes, get acceptance, close. From 1/1/2027 the Digital Transformation teams also run their projects in Halo.

lanes.name: XO / Project Controller
lanes.sub: Default controller is the client's XO

steps.title: Plan and staff
steps.note: Practice lead books resources in Halo
steps.detail: The practice lead books resources against the Halo project. Conflicts and over-allocation are resolved at the weekly Monday capacity meeting.

steps.title: Client kickoff
steps.who: XO leads; delivery owner presents the plan
steps.detail: The XO runs the kickoff (relationship, scope, contacts, communication plan) and the delivery owner presents the delivery plan and staffing.

steps.title: Deliver and log time
steps.note: Time in Halo; expenses in Paylocity
steps.detail: Resources log time daily against Halo project tasks; expenses go through Paylocity and sync to Halo for billing. The delivery owner sends client status reports at the cadence set in the SOW (weekly if the SOW does not say).

steps.title: Change order
steps.who: XO quotes; Partner (Account Executive Owner) signs
steps.flag: The Partner (Account Executive Owner) signs every change order before it reaches the client.
steps.detail: Change orders are quoted in Halo and sent by e-signature with the Partner signing before the client.

steps.title: Client accepts deliverables?
steps.detail: Formal client acceptance is required to close. The client's written approval (an email is enough) is recorded on the Halo project.

6.2.2.title: Manage customer service problems, requests, and inquiries
6.2.2.summary: Support tickets in Halo for two service models: Managed Technology clients (managed, co-managed, NOC and endpoint management), worked by a dispatcher and Tier 1 to 3 plus Centralized Services engineers; and large enterprise clients, where the Service Desk practice is Tier 1 and escalates to the client's own IT.

lanes.name: Service Desk practice
lanes.sub: Tier 1, Process Leads, Service Managers (enterprise clients)

steps.title: Ticket created
steps.note: Email, portal, phone or NinjaOne alert
steps.detail: Email and the Halo client portal create Halo tickets automatically, and NinjaOne RMM alerts create tickets automatically. Phone calls (Dialpad) are logged as tickets by the service desk; there is no Dialpad integration.

steps.title: Dispatch: triage and assign
steps.detail: The dedicated Managed Technology dispatcher categorizes and prioritizes each ticket and assigns it to Tier 1.

steps.title: Approve billable work
steps.detail: The XO approves the quote or T&M estimate, then the client accepts it in Halo, before out-of-scope work starts.

steps.title: Escalate to client IT
steps.detail: The Service Desk practice has no Tier 2/3: escalations go to the client's own resources through the existing integration with the client's ITSM platform. Do not change those integration runbooks.

steps.title: CSAT survey sent
steps.detail: Halo sends a CSAT survey when a ticket closes.

9.2.2.title: Invoice customer
9.2.2.summary: XO or Project Controller approves time and invoices; Finance (Next Level Now) spot-checks the run; the AR Clerk sends approved invoices from Halo with Avalara tax; invoices then sync to QuickBooks Online.

steps.title: Submit time and expenses
steps.detail: Each week's time (Halo) and expenses (Paylocity) are due by end of day Friday. Expenses flow from Paylocity into Halo through the planned integration so billable ones land on the invoice.
steps.flag: Time and expenses are due by end of day Friday each week.

steps.title: Approve billable time
steps.flag: Billable time is approved by the Project Controller / XO.

steps.title: Draft invoices generated
steps.note: Time, recurring, licensing, expenses; Avalara tax
steps.detail: Halo generates draft invoices. The Pax8 integration updates recurring licensing quantities and amounts automatically, and Avalara calculates final sales tax on the Halo invoice.

steps.title: Invoice correct?
steps.detail: The XO or Project Controller reviews each draft invoice because they know the project best.

steps.title: Spot-check invoice run
steps.detail: After XO approval, Finance reviews the invoice run summary (totals and exceptions) and sends anything questionable back to the XO before invoices go out.

steps.title: Run and send invoices
steps.detail: The AR Clerk runs only XO-approved invoices and sends them to clients from Halo.

steps.title: Sync to QuickBooks Online
steps.note: QBO + Avalara file and remit tax

9.2.3.title: Process accounts receivable (AR)
9.2.3.summary: Clients pay by ACH or check; payments are matched from the QuickBooks Online bank feed, applied and reconciled, and paid status syncs back to Halo. The Next Level Now controller reviews AR aging monthly with the XOs. Invoices still unpaid after their due date go to collections.

lanes.name: AR
lanes.sub: AR Clerk with Next Level Now

steps.title: Paid by due date?
steps.detail: Payments arrive by ACH or check.

steps.title: Payment received
steps.note: ACH or check, matched from the bank feed
steps.detail: Clients pay by ACH or check; payments are matched from the bank feed in QuickBooks Online. A client payment portal using Alternative Payments is planned for a later date.

steps.title: Paid status to Halo
steps.detail: The Halo–QuickBooks Online integration writes paid status back to Halo, so XOs see payment status on the client in Halo.
steps.note: Integration writes paid status to Halo

steps.title: Month-end AR aging review
steps.who: Next Level Now controller, with XOs
steps.detail: The Next Level Now controller runs the month-end AR aging review; XOs review their own past-due accounts.

9.2.4.title: Manage and process collections
9.2.4.span: Past due → paid, plan or write-off
9.2.4.summary: Automated QuickBooks Online reminders first (Net 30, then +15 to +90 days); the XO steps in at 45+ days past the due date and the account's Executive Owner (EO) at 60+; at 90+ the Managing Partner over Operations and the EO approve any credit hold, and the CEO approves write-offs.

lanes.name: AR
lanes.sub: AR Clerk with Next Level Now

steps.title: Send reminders
steps.detail: Planned QuickBooks Online setup (not yet configured): invoices are Net 30, with automated reminders at 15, 30, 45, 60 and 90 days past due. The 90-day reminder warns that service may be cancelled.

steps.title: Paid within 45 days of due date?
XO contacts client
steps.flag: The XO is the first escalation once an invoice is 45+ days past its due date.

steps.title: Paid within 60 days of due date?
EO engages client executive
steps.flag: The account's Executive Owner (EO) gets involved at 60+ days past the invoice due date.

steps.title: Credit hold or suspension
steps.who: Managing Partner, Operations and the account EO
steps.detail: At 90+ days past due, after the final warning, the Managing Partner over Operations and the account EO jointly approve a credit hold or service suspension.

steps.title: Approve write-off
steps.detail: The CEO currently approves every write-off (no dollar threshold); the Controller posts it in QuickBooks Online.

5.2.title: Manage service delivery resources
5.2.span: Deal reaches Proposal → people assigned in Halo
5.2.summary: Project staffing: practice leads review pipeline demand at the weekly Monday capacity meeting chaired by the Managing Partner over Operations, borrow across practices before using a subcontractor, and assign named people to Halo tasks once the XO accepts the handoff. Service desk staffing is planned separately (6.2.1).

lanes.name: Monday capacity meeting
lanes.sub: Practice leads, chaired by Managing Partner, Operations

steps.title: Review pipeline and capacity
steps.detail: Each Monday the practice leads and the Managing Partner over Operations review deals at Proposal and current bookings. The planning horizon is not defined yet; four weeks is the likely standard.

steps.title: Borrow from another practice
steps.detail: Before going outside, the meeting agrees a loan of people or skills from another practice.

steps.title: Engage a subcontractor
steps.detail: The practice lead decides on a subcontractor within the project budget.

steps.title: Tier and vet before any access
steps.detail: Per the Vendor Management Policy, the subcontractor is risk-tiered and through due diligence before getting any access to Sparkhound or client systems.

steps.title: Pencil in the team
steps.note: Noted; not booked in Halo yet
steps.detail: The planned team is noted at the meeting. Nothing is booked in Halo until the deal is won.

steps.title: Assign named people to Halo tasks
steps.note: Hours and dates; PTO checked by hand
steps.detail: Once the XO accepts the handoff (3.5.4), the practice lead assigns named people to the Halo project tasks with hours and dates. PTO is approved in Paylocity and taken into account by hand.

9.5.1.title: Report time
9.5.1.summary: Managed Services and Digital Transformation operations teams log time weekly in Halo, due Friday end of day; sales, admin and HR don't enter time. Halo reminds anyone late and the practice lead follows up Monday. Hourly staff also enter pay hours in Paylocity. Approved time is locked and feeds invoicing and utilization.

lanes.name: Delivery staff
lanes.sub: Managed Services and Digital Transformation operations teams

steps.title: Start: work done during the week
Log time against Halo tickets and tasks
steps.who: Managed Services and Digital Transformation operations teams
steps.flag: Time and expenses are due by end of day Friday each week.
steps.detail: Delivery staff log their week against Halo tickets and project tasks by Friday end of day. Most staff are salaried, so Halo time drives billing and utilization, not pay. Sales, admin and HR do not enter time.

steps.title: Enter pay hours in Paylocity
steps.note: Hourly staff; also log work in Halo
steps.detail: Hourly employees enter their hours in Paylocity for pay and also log the work in Halo so it can be billed and counted for utilization.

steps.title: All time in by Friday EOD?
Remind and follow up
steps.detail: Halo sends an automatic reminder to anyone with missing time; the practice lead follows up on Monday with anyone still missing.

steps.title: Approve timesheets for completeness
steps.flag: Practice lead approves each timesheet for completeness by Monday end of day; the XO then approves billable time on their clients before invoicing.
steps.detail: The practice lead approves each timesheet for completeness and, for hourly staff, checks that Halo and Paylocity hours roughly match. Approval is inconsistent today; this is the proposed standard.

steps.title: Approve billable time
steps.flag: Practice lead approves each timesheet for completeness by Monday end of day; the XO then approves billable time on their clients before invoicing.
steps.detail: The XO or Project Controller approves billable time on their clients before invoices are generated (9.2.2).

steps.title: Approved time locked
steps.detail: Once approved, time cannot be edited unless the approver reopens it.

9.2.2.S1.title: Set up and maintain recurring agreements
9.2.2.S1.summary: Managed services agreements bill monthly in advance from Halo. Microsoft license lines change monthly through the Pax8 sync; managed seats and services change only at the quarterly QBR, from the client's user access review, and that rate holds for the next three months.
questions: Confirm that Halo creates the recurring agreement and invoice automatically from the accepted quote.

steps.title: Agreement and recurring invoice created
steps.detail: Halo is believed to create the recurring agreement and invoice automatically when the quote is accepted; to be confirmed.

steps.title: Check the agreement against the SOW
steps.detail: The XO checks services, quantities and prices on the new agreement match the signed SOW.

steps.title: Bill monthly in advance
steps.detail: Each month the recurring invoice bills that month's managed services in advance through the 9.2.2 invoice run.

steps.title: License lines updated from Pax8
steps.detail: Microsoft license changes, made by the client in Pax8 or by Tier 2 from a Halo ticket, sync to the license lines automatically and hit the next monthly invoice.

steps.title: Hold the quarterly QBR
steps.detail: Each quarter the XO meets the client for a business review that includes the user access review.

steps.title: Confirm users in the access review
steps.detail: The client confirms its active users as part of the quarterly user access review; that count sets the per-user quantity.

steps.title: Update seats and services
steps.detail: The XO updates per-user quantities from the confirmed user count, plus any services added or dropped, which also wait for the QBR. The client pays that rate for the next three months.

steps.title: End: next quarter billed at the new rate (9.2.2)

5.4.1.S1.title: Onboard new managed services clients
5.4.1.S1.summary: The XO runs Sparkhound's onboarding project from a Halo template: kickoff with the client sets a go-live date about 30 days out, access is set up and vaulted in Hudu, the technical team does discovery, agent deployment and documentation, and a communication campaign tells end users how to get support. A one-time onboarding fee is billed up front; recurring billing starts at go-live.
questions: Does anyone confirm onboarding is complete before go-live, and who?

steps.title: Create the project from the onboarding template
Invoice the onboarding fee
steps.detail: The one-time onboarding fee is billed up front through the invoice run (9.2.2); monthly services start at go-live.

steps.title: Kickoff and agree the go-live date
steps.detail: At the kickoff meeting the XO proposes a go-live date from the plan's timeline and tasks, generally about 30 days out, and the team works toward it.

steps.title: Collect and rotate credentials from the outgoing provider
Discovery, agents and documentation
steps.detail: Tier 2/3 engineers run discovery and document the environment in Hudu; Centralized Services deploys tooling and agents.

steps.title: Go-live communications to end users
steps.note: Who to call, how tickets work
steps.detail: A communication campaign leads up to go-live so every end user knows the date, how to reach the service desk and how tickets work.

steps.title: Confirm onboarding is complete
steps.detail: Proposed: the XO confirms the plan's tasks are done (agents deployed, Hudu documentation complete, contacts in Halo) before go-live.

steps.title: End: supported by the service desk (6.2.2)

9.3.2.S1.title: Close the month
9.3.2.S1.summary: Next Level Now closes the books in QuickBooks Online by business day 5: invoices and payroll sync in, bank and card accounts reconciled, bills and accruals entered. The CEO and the Managing Partner over Operations review the P&L and balance sheet before the close is final, and the period is then locked. Revenue is recognized as invoiced.

steps.title: Prepare P&L and balance sheet
steps.detail: Next Level Now prepares the monthly P&L and balance sheet by business day 5. Revenue is recognized as invoiced, with no deferral.

steps.title: CEO and MP Ops approve?
steps.detail: The CEO and the Managing Partner over Operations review the statements; questions go back to Next Level Now to adjust before the close is final.

3.5.2.S2.title: Manage contract renewals
3.5.2.S2.span: 90 days before term end → renewed or offboarding
3.5.2.S2.summary: Managed services agreements auto-renew. Ninety days before term end a Halo ticket prompts the XO to review the agreement and propose the year's increase within the contract's annual cap; the Managing Partner over Operations approves it, and the XO tells the client the increase or that there is none. A client who gives notice is escalated for retention before offboarding.

steps.title: Renewal ticket to the XO
steps.note: New; to set up in Halo
steps.detail: No reminder exists today. Halo will raise a renewal ticket to the XO 90 days before the agreement end date.

steps.title: Review the agreement and propose the year's increase
steps.detail: Current contracts allow a price increase each year up to a set percentage. The XO reviews the agreement and proposes this year's increase, or none.

steps.title: Approve the increase or no change
steps.detail: The Managing Partner over Operations decides any renewal price change case by case.

steps.title: Tell the client this year's increase
steps.detail: Each year the XO tells the client in writing what the increase is, or that there is no increase.

steps.title: Client gives notice not to renew?
Try to retain the client
steps.who: XO with Partner / Managing Partner, Operations

3.3.3.S1.title: Approve quote pricing and discounts
3.3.3.S1.span: Partner prices a quote → quote continues
3.3.3.S1.summary: Service line owners set each item's street price and floor in the Halo price book every year, approved by the Managing Partner over Operations. The Partner may discount freely down to the floor; a quote below the floor needs the Managing Partner over Operations' approval before it goes out.

steps.title: Price from the Halo price book
steps.note: Street price and floor per item
steps.detail: Service line owners review street prices and floors annually and the Managing Partner over Operations approves the price book. The Partner may discount freely between street price and floor.

steps.title: Hold the quote for approval
steps.flag: Quotes priced below the floor are held in Halo until the Managing Partner over Operations approves them.
steps.detail: Proposed design: a Halo quote approval rule stops a below-floor quote from being sent until approved. Today the request is informal.

steps.title: End: re-price at or above the floor (3.5.3)

9.6.1.title: Process accounts payable
9.6.1.span: Vendor sends a bill → paid and reconciled
9.6.1.summary: Vendors send bills to the AP inbox and Next Level Now enters them in QuickBooks Online. New vendors and bank-detail changes are verified by a call-back first. The budget owner approves each bill, Next Level Now prepares a weekly payment run that the CEO approves and releases, and pass-through costs (Pax8, distributor hardware) are reconciled to Halo billings each month.

lanes.name: Budget owner
lanes.sub: Whoever bought it, or their leader

steps.title: Receive in the AP inbox and enter the bill
New vendor or changed bank details?
Verify by call-back to a known contact
steps.detail: Before a new vendor's bank details are set up, or any change is used, Next Level Now calls a known contact at the vendor to confirm them.

steps.title: Approve and release the payment run
Reconcile pass-through costs
steps.detail: Each month, Pax8 license and distributor hardware costs are reconciled to what was billed in Halo, catching costs that were never billed.
